best.plan_strategy: Attempt 2: stay on the ranking axis but attack the 0.2509 train_val_gap with a heavily regularised, low-capacity gradient-boosted fit. Same family (hist_gbdt) and same NaN-native preprocessing so the movement is attributable to capacity alone: 600 iterations at learning_rate 0.03, max_leaf_nodes 8, min_samples_leaf 60, l2_regularization 10.0, max_depth 4, early_stopping off so all 5,026 train rows are used, class_weight held at 'balanced' so the operating point is unchanged from iteration 1. Read roc_auc, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut and train_val_gap: if the shrunken model's ranking ceiling rises above 0.7836 the variance was costing ranking and the next attempt pushes further in that direction (or into xgboost with subsample/reg_lambda); if the ceiling does not move, the ranking is family-limited and attempts 3-5 go to xgboost and a bagging family instead.

critic.evidence: Iteration 1 (hist_gbdt, 400 iters, lr 0.06, 31 leaves, l2 1.0, impute none, class_weight balanced) scored val balanced_accuracy 0.7491 (95% CI 0.7222~0.7785) against the bar 0.8399 — a shortfall of 0.0908. train_balanced_accuracy is 1.0 with train_val_gap 0.250885: the model memorised all 5,026 train rows, so its ranking (roc_auc 0.8587, balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7836) is capacity-limited by variance, not by too little capacity. The operating point is nearly spent: cut_headroom is only 0.034485 of the 0.0908 still needed (38%), and recall 0.5761 vs specificity 0.9221 means class_weight='balanced' has already been applied yet still leaves recall the lower arm — but even the best possible cut of this ranking (0.7836) falls 0.0563 short of the bar, so the remaining 62% is ranking. Only one family has been tried (span of family maxima is undefined with n=1), and dropped_hyperparams is empty, so every setting above was really applied. Train time 11.2 s leaves plenty of budget; 4 iterations remain.
critic.direction: Stay in hist_gbdt but attack the 0.2509 train_val_gap by cutting capacity and adding regularisation — lower learning rate with fewer, shallower, better-populated leaves and much stronger L2 — changing only hyperparameters (family and preprocessing held fixed at impute:'none', class_weight:'balanced') so the next row attributes its movement to capacity alone and tells us how much of the 0.0563 ranking gap variance was costing.

critic.evidence: Iteration 2 (hist_gbdt, 600 iters, lr 0.03, 8 leaves, depth 4, min_samples_leaf 60, l2 10.0, class_weight 'balanced', impute none) scored val balanced_accuracy 0.7725 (95% CI 0.7460~0.7987) against the bar 0.8399 — still 0.0674 short. dropped_hyperparams is empty, so the whole capacity cut was applied: train_val_gap fell 0.2509 → 0.1190 and train_balanced_accuracy 1.0 → 0.8915, i.e. the memorisation was genuinely removed, yet the ranking did not move — roc_auc 0.8587 → 0.8552 and balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7836 → 0.7795 both went slightly *down*, and pr_auc 0.6118 → 0.5952. The paired Δ vs iteration 1 is +0.0234 with 95% CI -0.0020~+0.0503 (P 0.970), so even the balanced_accuracy movement is not resolved by these rows, and iteration 1's 0.7491 sits inside this attempt's CI (width 0.0528). That answers the question the plan posed: variance was not what limited the ranking, so overfitting is now spent as a diagnosis (it was prescribed once and bought nothing separable from 0). The operating point is also spent — cut_headroom is 0.006974 against the 0.0674 still needed (10%), with recall 0.7536 vs specificity 0.7914 now nearly equal, so class_weight has essentially nothing left; ~90% of the shortfall is in the ranking, and even this ranking's best possible cut (0.7795) falls 0.0604 short of the bar. Two hist_gbdt attempts have covered ranking ceilings of only 0.7836 and 0.7795 (span 0.0041) while the shortfall is 0.0674 — the bar is above this baseline-class ranking's ceiling, so only a materially better ranking generator can reach it, not another point in this family's hyperparameter space. calibration_error also degraded 0.0646 → 0.1555 and brier 0.1027 → 0.1391 under the heavy shrinkage. Cost is a non-issue: 8.0 s train, 10.6 s wall, 3 iterations left.
critic.direction: Stop tuning hist_gbdt capacity — the gap closed without the ranking moving — and switch family to xgboost at moderate capacity with row/column subsampling (a different ranking generator, still NaN-native so preprocessing stays impute:'none' and the family is the only lever that moves), keeping class_weight/scale_pos_weight at the balanced point since recall 0.7536 and specificity 0.7914 are already nearly equal.

concrete_changes.scale_pos_weight: balanced_ratio (positives:negatives frequency ratio, same operating point as class_weight='balanced')

critic.evidence: Iteration 3 (xgboost, 800 trees, lr 0.05, depth 6, subsample 0.8, reg_lambda 2.0, scale_pos_weight 5.07, impute 'none'; dropped_hyperparams empty, so everything applied) scored val balanced_accuracy 0.7226 (95% CI 0.6954~0.7560) against the bar 0.8399 — 0.1173 short, and the paired Δ vs iteration 2 is -0.0499 (95% CI -0.0763~-0.0215, P(better) 0.000), a resolved regression: the family swap I prescribed last time paid negatively. Crucially it did not move the ranking either — balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut went 0.7795 → 0.7848 while roc_auc went 0.8552 → 0.8605, both inside the 0.003–0.006 paired resolution for roc_auc; the two families tried now span balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut 0.7836~0.7848 (width 0.0012) while the distance from the best cut of the best ranking to the bar is 0.0551, i.e. 46× that span (KS 0.5696 vs the 0.6798 the bar requires). That is why I am not issuing wrong_model_family a third time: it has now been prescribed once, cost a resolved -0.0499, and the family-maxima span it would need to exploit is 46× too small — one more estimator off the same list cannot cover 0.1173. What did move is variance: xgboost went back to train_balanced_accuracy 1.0 with train_val_gap 0.2774 (vs iteration 2's 0.8915 / 0.1190), and its cut landed badly — recall 0.5109 vs specificity 0.9343 despite scale_pos_weight 5.07, leaving cut_headroom 0.0622, 53% of the 0.1173 still needed. So half the shortfall is a mis-placed operating point that a stronger positive weight can reclaim on the ranking already in hand, and the other 47% sits in a ranking that neither family nor capacity tuning has moved across three attempts on 5,026 train rows with a 5.07:1 imbalance and only the raw card columns available (no feature construction is possible here) — the limit is the information in the data, not the estimator.
critic.direction: With 2 iterations left, stop swapping families (the two tried span only 0.0012 of best-cut ranking) and spend the attempts harvesting the one lever with measurable size: go back to the best ranking generator (hist_gbdt, iteration 2's regularised settings, impute 'none') and push the positive class weight past the 'balanced' point — recall 0.5109 sat far below specificity 0.9343 at scale_pos_weight 5.07 and iteration 2's balanced point already had recall 0.7536 vs specificity 0.7914, so an explicit weight of roughly 7:1 should equalise the two arms and cash in the 0.0622 cut_headroom, while adding missing_count as the only pipeline change is deliberately deferred so the weight move stays attributable.
